subject: Tenant activation: VPC & firewall validation for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>, GCP Sales <gcp-sales@google.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Tenant activation: VPC & firewall validation for Nimbus Health

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the kickoff call earlier. As discussed, I attached a compact activation checklist that covers the minimum items we need from your infra team to get a private tenant (VPC / on-prem connectivity) ready for Redwood Private. Quick highlights:

- Account & IAM: Service account with roles + email for audit events
- Network: VPC peering or dedicated interconnect details, route tables, CIDR ranges
- Firewall: Allowlist for control plane + worker egress (sample ports in attached fw-sample-rules.txt)
- KMS: Customer-managed key or KMS ARN for secrets at rest
- Access: Service account key exchange, bastion IPs for troubleshooting (if applicable)
- Test plan: Basic smoke tests + a dry-run date

Attachments: activation-checklist-v1.xlsx, fw-sample-rules.txt (see bottom of checklist for port rationale).

As next steps, can you confirm:
1) Preferred connectivity method (VPC peering vs interconnect)
2) An initial CIDR range we can expect for the Redwood interfaces
3) A security contact and a procurement contact so we can line up the SOW/PO cadence

Target for dry-run: Wed, Jul 15 — if that window looks ok we'll confirm a 10:00 PDT slot.

Thanks,

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Sr. Manager, Customer Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Jul 2025 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant activation: VPC & firewall validation for Nimbus Health

Thanks Sean — received and reviewed. A few clarifying questions before we lock the dry-run:

- Connectivity: We're planning to do a Cloud Interconnect (dedicated). Expected public CIDR for the peering side is 10.240.0.0/16; are there any reserved ranges you need us to avoid?
- Firewall: Can you confirm whether Redwood's control plane uses ephemeral outbound ports or a fixed range? Our security team prefers fixed ranges for appliance rules.
- KMS: We use GCP KMS and can provide a key ARN once our security lead gives the green light.

Also looping procurement — what format do you prefer for the reserved capacity SOW, and is there an initial acceptance checklist we should attach to the PO?

Appreciate the checklist doc.

—Alex Ruiz
Alex Ruiz, Infrastructure Lead
Nimbus Health

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tenant activation: VPC & firewall validation for Nimbus Health

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick reply and good questions. Short answers below, then a proposed task list for the next 48 hours.

- Reserved ranges: Redwood control plane expects the customer to allow outgoing to our managed IPs; we do not require unique private CIDR beyond avoiding the 10.128.0.0/9 blocks we reserve internally. Your 10.240.0.0/16 looks fine.
- Ports: Control-plane uses a stable set of TCP/443 and TCP/9443 between worker nodes and control endpoints; worker egress is NATed and can use ephemeral ports but we list them in fw-sample-rules.txt for convenience. If your security team insists on fixed ranges for egress, we can provide a /24 ephemeral egress pool as a concession for the acceptance window.
- KMS: GCP KMS is fine. Send the key resource name once procurement is ready.

Proposed 48-hour task list (owners):
- Kimberly: Draft firewall rules tailored to Nimbus (attach to this thread) — owner: kimberly_park@redwood.com
- Marissa: Coordinate KMS/secret policy and confirm key ARN (owner: marissa_cole@redwood.com)
- Alex/Procurement: Confirm SOW format and PO timing
- Sean: Schedule dry-run and provide smoke test checklist

I'll schedule the dry-run tentatively for Wed Jul 15 10:00 PDT and will send a calendar invite once you confirm. Also uploaded a short guide to the activation checklist here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2b3Cactivation

—Sean

Alex / team — attaching a tailored firewall fragment for Nimbus based on your CIDR and interconnect plan. The attached file (fw-rules-nimbus-rcpt-20250713.txt) includes:

- Control plane allowlist: 3 IPs (tcp/443, tcp/9443)
- Worker egress sample: NATed egress to 0.0.0.0/0 with recommended outbound timeouts
- Bastion access: explicit /32 allow for troubleshooting windows

Please review and confirm. If procurement needs a shorter list to include with a PO we can provide a one-page acceptance checklist.

attachment: fw-rules-nimbus-rcpt-20250713.txt (text)

—Kimberly

Alex / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps from Redwood's side:

- KMS: We're good to accept a GCP KMS key ARN. Please send the resource name via secure ticket (we'll add it to the account configuration).
- Dry-run: Confirmed for Wed Jul 15 10:00 PDT — calendar invite sent. Plan: 30-minute smoke run (connectivity, model load, basic inference), followed by 30-minute validation window.
- Acceptance items to attach to PO: brief 1-page activation checklist (I attached to the invite).

We'll watch the firewall rule test during the dry-run — Kimberly will be on the call for live troubleshooting. If procurement wants a sample SOW, Procurement, please ping my team and we'll surface our template.

See you tomorrow.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Onboarding)
Redwood Inference
